back: A one-to-many dependency: when the subject changes, all registered observers are notified automatically.
One method, usually update(event), called by the subject on each change.
Push sends the data with the notification. Pull only signals a change; observers query the subject.
Observers never detached stay referenced by the subject, leaking memory and receiving stale events.

front: Why iterate over a copy in notify()?
back: So an observer can detach itself (or others) during notification without skipping anyone.
Observer: subject calls observers directly. Pub/sub: a broker decouples publishers and subscribers.
Loose coupling: the subject depends only on the observer interface, never on concrete listeners.
A list of callables; subscribe() returns an unsubscribe function.
A plain loop stops, so later observers miss the event. Isolate, collect, or fail fast on purpose.
